sources.title: Library of Congress: Country Profile, Nepal (November 2005)
sources.note: Historical background, printed pages 2 to 4. Used for eighteenth-century state formation and Rana government, not current political institutions. Outdated ancient chronology and evaluative generalizations omitted.

sources.title: District Tehri Garhwal: History
sources.note: Official district history: Gorkha invasion in 1803, victory and establishment of dominion, followed by Company intervention and Tehri state from 1815. Used to expose premature 1783 western geometry; no endorsement of modern boundary claims.

sources.title: National Army Museum: The Gurkhas
sources.note: Opening historical section: East India Company war 1814 to 1816 and recruitment from 1815. Museum shorthand calling Gorkha a city-state is not repeated; hereditary martial stereotypes omitted.

sources.title: Deepak Thapa: Nepal’s war and political transition, a brief history
sources.note: Conciliation Resources, Accord 26: historical political transitions, 1960 takeover/1962 Panchayat constitution, 1990 movement, 1996 war, peace and republican transition. Researcher analysis; no endorsement of any faction.

sources.title: United Nations Security Council briefing on Nepal, November 2008
sources.note: Contemporary UN briefing: 2006 end of decade-long war and May 2008 abolition of monarchy. Used for 2008 transition and institutional continuity.

sources.title: Constitution of Nepal, 2015: English text at WIPO Lex
sources.note: Original 2015 constitutional text: opening/date; Articles 2 to 8 and 56; Schedule 1; Article 307. Historical text, not legal advice or certification of every current amendment. Combine underlying work budget with Nepali text.

sources.title: Nepal Law Commission: नेपालको संविधान
sources.note: Official repository indexed title and Article 307(1); publication date 2072.06.03. Current direct fetch failed, full indexed original shows exact title. English parallel checked in WIPO constitutional title/Article 307. Romanization is an editorial transliteration of modern Nepali, not another historical inscription.

sources.title: Francis Buchanan Hamilton: An Account of the Kingdom of Nepal (1819)
sources.note: Original public-domain book: introduction explains visit in 1802 to 1803 and local informants; printed pages 38 to 40 on Newar houses and Crawford architectural notes; pages 232 to 233 on metal vessels and bark paper. A colonial observer with prejudices, not a universal household survey. Racial and religious slurs and sweeping character judgments omitted.

sources.title: Nepal Tourism Board: Culture, Food section
sources.note: Contemporary Food subsection only: dal, bhat, tarkari, achar, momos, roti and dhedo. Sweeping claims elsewhere about all Nepalis, gender roles, caste, beef or menstrual practices omitted.

sources.title: Nepal Tourism Board: Dashain
sources.note: Family visits, tika, gifts, new clothes, feasts, kite flying and village swings. A Hindu festival, not universal national religious practice. Malformed/current calendar date labels not repeated.

sources.title: UNESCO: Weaving the future, Tharu women’s craft in Lumbini
sources.note: 30 September 2025 interviews: Panmati Tharuni learned at twelve; grass basket materials/functions and teaching by relatives. Contemporary named community evidence, not eighteenth-century practice projected backward.

sources.title: UNICEF: Communicating for change
sources.note: 28 June 2019: Dev Laxmi Malla in Mugu, March training, handbook/photos and mothers’ group; fathers’ groups and SMS. Numbers and practices dated to report, no universal clinical outcome claim.

sources.title: WHO: Tilganga Institute recognized as a collaborating centre
sources.note: 21 July 2019 report: inauguration in 1994, cataract training, eye bank and intraocular lens export. Avoid promotional cumulative figures and attributing all national blindness reduction to one institution.

sources.title: UNICEF: Good for everyone
sources.note: 2022 report at Bhanu Secondary School: water storage/group washing, five toilets each for girls/boys and one accessible toilet, sanitary pads and students’ feedback. One school and one-star progress, not universal complete sanitation.

sources.title: UNICEF: Sparking possibilities
sources.note: 3 January 2024: Afsana Khatun, Parsa; nine-month SAGE programme, music/games/drama; completion in 2022 and school enrollment. Contradictory first girl in family claim omitted because source also says sister dropped out and Afsana previously attended madrasa.

sources.title: UNESCO: Rescue archaeology after Nepal’s earthquakes
sources.note: 12 January 2016, report on October to November 2015 work: radar, excavations, early timber/clay platform under Patan Char Narayan, Kasthamandap foundations undamaged. Do not date earlier material to Shah rule or claim every monument survived.

sources.title: JAXA: Four CubeSats deployed from Kibo
sources.note: 25 June 2019 account of deployment on 17 June; NepaliSat-1 co-developed by NAST/Kyutech in BIRDS-3, ten-centimeter cube. Space-station deployment distinguished from earlier rocket launch.

sources.title: UN special procedures: Nepal communication NPL 1/2025
sources.note: Communication dated 8 January 2026, concerns allegations about killings, detention and excessive force during 8 to 9 September 2025 demonstrations. These are reported allegations, not final judicial findings. No current officeholder or unverified final death toll.

proposedOverrides.name: Nepal
proposedOverrides.summary: Nepal’s kingdom became a republic through conflict and political change.

batchIdentityNotes.finding: Exact missing indexed record 1783 to present, no existing card or staged collision. Sixteen decoded historical-basemap features; 1783 and 1800 bbox 76.287 to 88.231 E, 26.384 to 31.713 N; 1815 onward contracts west edge to about 80.099 E. Earlier western footprint prematurely includes Garhwal conquered after 1803; no exact yearly or current sovereignty claim. Historical foundation 1768 to 1769 is separate from map start. Phases distinguish Shah, Rana, royal Panchayat, multiparty/war, peace and republic. Final 2027 exclusive end is display coverage, not predicted political ending.

nepal (1200 to 1279), nepal-1492 (1492 to 1500) and nepal-1650 (1650 to 1700) remain separate, since earlier valley kingdoms do not share one continuous centralized state identity with post-conquest Nepal.
